entry_state: Insurance premium, service revenue and profit follow different schedules. Group measurement retains future service, incurred claims, risk adjustment and unearned profit separately. The two-year cases distinguish loss reversal from revenue and finance from service; the connected issued groups and reinsurance reconcile through year one, while year-two settlement is still being developed.
exit_state: The connected insurance groups reach the same final cash under histories with different recognition timing, while improper pooling hides losses. Complete event publication preserves group components and exact retries. PAA eligibility, acquisition-cost treatment, claim settlement and finance have distinct clocks; reinsurance and direct participation require their own contractual conditions. The next case values a participating guarantee.
findings: The connected-group example shows why final cash cannot validate initial group recognition or interim loss allocation.
The posting design distinguishes valid accounting, component state, atomic publication, retry and unknown acknowledgement; actual durability remains unimplemented.
PAA does not eliminate discounting of long-tail claims, and the LIC finance rate can differ from the group inception rate. No new confirmed manuscript defect.
